title: Fifteen Years of the Premier League: What Sustained Success Looks Like
summary: Fifteen seasons of Premier League data connect institutional persistence with fair comparison, attack–defence efficiency and the limits of simple discipline models.
key_takeaway: Dominance is balanced performance sustained over time: strong clubs score, control defensive downside and resist explanations built on one peripheral statistic.

inline_figures.caption: League-position points across fifteen seasons show a steep elite tier and a long tail of shorter or less successful top-flight records.
The efficiency map plots goals scored against goals conceded per game, with bubble size representing points per game.
The correlation matrix shows how wins, goal difference, attacking production and defensive control relate to points per game.
Champions' yellow-card trend and the league average vary across eras rather than revealing one stable discipline formula.
